title: Socio-Economic Practices of Early Humans
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 9 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Facts (to confirm): Olduvai Gorge (Tanzania), Olorgesailie and Kariandusi (Kenya); Early, Middle and Late Stone Age tools from heavy choppers to small blades. Draw tools rather than copy images.

skills.key_step: The child describes Stone Age ways of life and tools and names East African sites.
steps: Name the way of getting food: hunting and gathering.
Name the tools and how they changed.

board.do: Draw a heavy chopper and a small sharp blade.

board.say: Was this made earlier or later than the chopper?

misconceptions.ask: How did early Stone Age humans get food?
misconceptions.repair: Put hunting and gathering, then farming, on a timeline with the Stone Age periods.

misconceptions.ask: What were Stone Age tools made of?
misconceptions.repair: Compare a stone hand axe with an iron hoe and place each on a timeline.

misconceptions.ask: Which is a Stone Age site in East Africa?
misconceptions.repair: Sort sites by age: Stone Age sites (Olduvai, Olorgesailie) and later historic buildings (Fort Jesus).

misconceptions.ask: Did the earliest Stone Age humans use fire?
misconceptions.repair: Place "fire" later on the Stone Age timeline.

checks.question: How did early Stone Age humans get food?
Name a Stone Age site in East Africa.
